source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 736 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 736.

PD 736.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 736 was established by Ordinance No. 26178, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 14, 2005. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 736 is established on property located at the southwest intersection of Clark Road and Panavision Trail. The size of PD 736 is approximately 8.2 acres. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 736A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. [Editor’s note: The development plan and landscape plan approved by the city plan commission on December 15, 2005, were rescinded by Ordinance No. 26461.] (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this district are those main uses permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the TH-2(A) Townhouse District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) Private streets are permitted by right.

(c) Detached single family uses are prohibited. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) In this district, the following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) In this district, the following accessory use is permitted by right:

-- Accessory community center (private). (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is five feet.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, no minimum side yard is required. If a side yard is provided, the minimum setback is five feet.

(2) Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(3) Setbacks from the perimeter of the Property must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan.

(c) Setbacks from shared access areas. Minimum setback from a shared access area to the face of a garage is 10 feet. No other setback from a shared access area is required.

(d) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 78.

(e) Floor area. Maximum floor area for an accessory community center (private) is 1,200 square feet.

(f) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(g) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage on an individual lot is 80 percent. Maximum total lot coverage for the Property is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(h) Lot size. For single family uses, minimum lot size is 2,000 square feet.

(i) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is two and one-half. For purposes of this provision, a one-half story is a story wholly contained within the roofline of the structure or a story with a floor area of less than one-half the floor area of the story below it.

(j) Single family structure spacing. A minimum of 10 feet between each group of eight single family structures must be provided by plat. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided below, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For single family uses, two spaces for each dwelling unit must be provided on the lot and must be located within an enclosed structure.

(c) In addition to the parking spaces required in Subsection (b), a minimum of 0.25 parking spaces per dwelling unit must be provided on the Property. These parking spaces must be unassigned and available for visitors.

(d) In addition to the parking spaces required in Subsections (b) and (c), a minimum of one space per 300 square feet of floor area must be provided for an accessory community center (private) use.

(e) Off-street parking is not permitted in shared access areas or private streets, except that the off-street parking spaces required in Subsections (c) and (d) may be provided in the private street subject to the approval of the location of the spaces by the director of public works and transportation; the approved location of the spaces must be shown on the development plan.

(f) All garages must be equipped with automatic garage door openers with a backup power source in the event of disruption of local utilities. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Clark Road Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.110. CLARK ROAD IMPROVEMENTS.

Prior to the final inspection on the 25th single family structure, a left-turn lane with storage pocket on northbound Clark Road must be constructed to provide entrance to the Property, with final design and construction approved by the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided below, landscaping and tree preservation must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) A landscape plan must be submitted with the development plan before issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. The landscape plan must provide a minimum of three trees per lot, each a minimum caliper of two inches, with a minimum of one tree located on each lot. The trees must be species listed in Section 51A-10.134(b) or Mountain Laurel (Kalmia latifolia). Trees required by this subsection that are not planted on a lot must be planted in the areas labeled on the conceptual plan as common area A, B, C, or D, or in the private street parkway (i.e. within the street right-of-way but outside of paved portion of the street), or in the Clark Road parkway adjacent to the Property, subject to all city licensing and permit requirements. In addition to the tree planting requirements in this subsection, native trees must be preserved as indicated on the conceptual plan.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.113. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Subdivision signs. A maximum of two subdivision signs are permitted in the location shown on the conceptual plan. They may project a maximum of 12 inches from the surface of the structure and they may be constructed to the same height as the perimeter fencing up to a maximum height of seven feet.

(c) No parking signs. Signage must be in place prohibiting parking in the shared access area or private streets, except in those areas where parking is permitted under Section 51P-736.109(e). (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Fencing
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.114. FENCING.

(a) Except for the entryway area shown on the conceptual plan, fencing must be provided at a minimum height of six feet and a maximum height of seven feet in the locations shown on the conceptual plan.

(b) Maximum height of fencing in the entryway, as shown on the conceptual plan, inclusive of the gates, is seven feet.

(c) All fencing on the Property must comply with the visual obstruction regulations in Section 51A-4.602(d). (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Shared Access Areas And Private Streets
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.115. SHARED ACCESS AREAS AND PRIVATE STREETS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a shared access development must comply with the provisions of Section 51A-4.411.

(b) A maximum of 78 lots may be platted as a shared access development.

(c) There is no minimum or maximum number of shared access points.

(d) A preliminary plat for a shared access development must be considered by the city plan commission simultaneously or before consideration of a development plan.

(e) The inner loop drive shown on the conceptual plan may be provided as a private street, and the private street must meet the following minimum standards:

(1) a 30-foot-wide right-of-way with adjacent five-foot-wide sidewalks in the location shown on the conceptual plan; and

(2) a pavement width of 22 feet measured from back of curb to back of curb. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Platted Common Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.116. PLATTED COMMON AREA.

A minimum of 1.50 acres of platted common area must be provided and shown on an approved development plan. (Ord. Nos. 26178; 26461)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26178)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-736.119. ZONING MAP.

PD 736 is located on Zoning Map No. P-3. (Ord. 26178)
